chunks: A man came to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) at Basra with a parchment and said: 'O Commander of the Faithful, look at this parchment, for it contains advice.' So he looked into it, then looked at the face of the man and said: 'If you are truthful, we will remunerate you; if you are a liar, we will punish you; and if you wish that we release you, we shall release you.' The man said: 'Rather, release me, O Commander of the Faithful.'

When the man turned back, he said: 'O you community, confused after its Prophet! Indeed, had you prioritised the one whom God has prioritised, and pushed back the one whom God has pushed back, and placed the wilayah and inheritance where God has placed them, the Guardian of God would not be in need, nor would any portion of God's obligations be neglected, nor would two people differ regarding God's judgment, nor would the community dispute any of God's commands — except that the knowledge of all that is with us from the Book of God. Therefore, taste the evil consequences of what your own hands have sent before, and God is not in the least unjust to the servants, and they who act unjustly shall come to know the turning they shall be overturned with.'

key_terms.الْمُتَحَيِّرَةُ: The confused/bewildered — Imam Ali's pointed characterization of the post-prophetic community that strayed from divine guidance
key_terms.الْوِرَاثَةَ: Inheritance — here referring to the spiritual and political succession of the Prophet, not mere property inheritance
key_terms.الْوِلَايَةَ: Wilayah — the divinely designated authority and guardianship of the Imam; a core Shia theological concept
key_terms.فَرَائِضِ اللَّهِ: God's obligations — the legislated shares in inheritance law; the Imam possesses their correct interpretation
key_terms.وَلِيُّ اللَّهِ: The Guardian of God — referring to the Imam, whose needs must be met by the community

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about wilayah and the confusion of the community after the Prophet?
ai.summary: In this powerful narration, Imam Ali (AS) — during his governance in Basra — first demonstrates his characteristic balanced justice by offering a man who brought dubious advice three options: reward if truthful, punishment if lying, or release with no consequences. When the man chose release, the Imam delivered a searing address to the broader community, lamenting their confusion after the Prophet's death. He declared that if the community had upheld the divine designation of the Imam's wilayah (guardianship) and kept the inheritance of leadership where God had placed it, the Islamic community would have been free from internal disputes, injustice, and confusion — because the Imams possess comprehensive knowledge from the Quran to resolve every disagreement. The speech concludes by citing two Quranic verses (3:182 and 26:227), warning the wrongdoers of their ultimate accountability.

en.hubeali:
Abu Ali Al Ashary and Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Ahmad Bin Is’haq, from Sa’dan Bin Muslim, from someone else from our companions who said, 
‘A man came over to Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> at Al-Basra with a parchment, so he said, ‘O Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup>! Look into this parchment, for therein is advice’. So he<sup>asws</sup> looked into it, then looked at the face of the man, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If you are truthful we<sup>asws</sup> will remunerate you, and if you are a liar we<sup>asws</sup> will punish you, and if you like that we<sup>asws</sup> should release you, we<sup>asws</sup> shall release you’. So he said, ‘Release me, O Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup>’.

So when the man turned back, heasws said: ‘O you community (who is) confused after its Prophetsaww! But had you prioritised the oneasws whom Allahazwj has prioritised, and pushed back the one whom Allahazwj has Pushed back, and made the Wilayah and the inheritance where Allahazwj has Made it to be, the Guradiansasws of Allahazwj would not be needy, nor would a portion from the Obligations (legislated shares of inheritance) of Allahazwj been neglected, nor two (people) would have differed regarding the Judgements of Allahazwj, nor would the community have squabbled with regards to anything from the Commands of Allahazwj, except that the Knowledge of that is in ourasws possession from the Book of Allahazwj. Therefore, taste the evil consequences of [3:182] what your own hands have sent before and because Allah is not in the least unjust to the servants [26:227] and they who act unjustly shall come to know the turning they shall be Overturned with’.
en.sarwar: 1. Abu Ali al-Ash ‘ariy and al-Husayn from Muhammad have narrated from Ahmad ibn Ishaq from Sa‘d an ibn Muslim from more than one person of our people who has narrated the following: “A man in Basrah brought a Sahifah (a booklet) and said, ‘O ’Amir al-Mu’minin, look at this booklet; there is advice in it.’ He (the Imam) looked at it, then he looked at the face of the man and said, ’If you are truthful we compensate you; if you are not truthful we will penalize you, if you want us to release you we will release you.’ He said, ’Release me O ’Amir al-Mu’minin. ’

When the man left ’Amir al-Mu’minin said, ‘You are the confused nation after your Prophet. Had you given priority to what Allah has given priority, kept back what Allah has kept back, placed people who possess divine authority and who inherit divine authority as Allah has placed, people who possess divine authority would not become needy. Obligations ordained by Allah would not remain neglected, two people would not quarrel [about a command of Allah and a nation would not fight over a command of Allah] but that the knowledge thereof is with us in the book of Allah. So taste the evil consequences of what your hands have sent ahead of you. Allah is not unjust to the servants. Very soon the unjust will find to what kind of returning place they have returned.”’
